title: Learning to Relate to Previous Turns in Conversational Search

problem.claim: Conversational search queries depend strongly on conversation context, and historical queries can help expand the current query.

gap.claim: Previous queries are not uniformly related to or useful for expanding the current query.

contributions.claim: A method is proposed to select historical queries relevant and useful to the current query.
A pseudo-labeling approach annotates useful historical queries according to their impact on retrieval results, enabling selector-model training despite limited labeled data.
A multi-task learning framework jointly trains the selector and retriever during fine-tuning to mitigate inconsistency between pseudo-labels and the changed retriever.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present their historical-query selection approach as a new method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four conversational search datasets are reported to demonstrate effectiveness and broad applicability compared with several strong baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Conversational search involves multiple interaction turns, and current queries depend strongly on conversation context.
Historical-query expansion can improve retrieval, but some previous queries are unrelated or unhelpful.
The method selects useful historical queries using pseudo-labels based on retrieval impact and trains a selection model.
A multi-task framework jointly fine-tunes the selector and retriever to address pseudo-label and retriever inconsistency.
The authors report experiments across four conversational search datasets against strong baselines.

source_observation.claim: Historical information can improve conversational retrieval, but its usefulness varies by query.

interpretation.claim: Context selection may be preferable to indiscriminate use of all available conversational history.

application.claim: Design retrieval systems that identify and use only history relevant to the current query.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy helps outside conversational search.

source_observation.claim: Pseudo-labels are derived from the impact of historical-query selection on retrieval results.

interpretation.claim: Retrieval outcomes can provide training signals when manually labeled selection data are scarce.

application.claim: Use outcome-based pseudo-labeling to train intermediate selection components in low-label settings.

exception.claim: Pseudo-label quality and the conditions under which it transfers to other retrievers are not specified.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the selection model, retriever architecture, or training details.
The abstract does not quantify the effect of pseudo-label and retriever inconsistency.
